text:
sec-bot: ALERT: ingestion pipeline uploaded a KMS-wrapped blob flagged by secrets-scanner — potential plaintext AWS keys inside. bucket=gs://partner-logs/2026-03-23/ingest-9a4f.enc ; kms_key=projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/ingest-wrap :rotating_light:

nina: @devon @sam oncall — can you triage? I see decrypt metadata shows our KMS key id. :eyes:

devon: looking now. initial note: ciphertext metadata says server-side wrap with our key (ingest-wrap). file looks like a single payload from partner ingestion job at 03:14 UTC. suspect partner posted plaintext that our ingest service wrapped (not client-wrap). possible leaked SA used by partner ci.

sam: if server-side wrap was used our service performed the wrap, so the source of plaintext is upstream. we need to assume the plaintext existed in transit/storage before wrapping. will search CI and logs for exposures.

nina: immediate containment checklist (short):
- revoke any suspected service-account keys that partner uses (devon)
- create new key-version for ingest-wrap and make it primary (devon)
- start rewrap job to re-encrypt stored secrets under new key-version (devon + sam)
- patch CI/pipeline to stop logging raw payloads and add redaction (sam)
- forward all KMS decrypt events for this key to security sink and increase retention to 90d (elisabeth)
- partner notification + legal hold (nina)

devon: performing revocation now. command I ran (sanitized):
```
# delete compromised SA key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123abcd --iam-account=svc-partner-ingest@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Creating new SA key and rotating bindings; adding temporary deny policy to prevent further writes from partner pipeline until we validate.

devon: for KMS rotation plan: create a new key version and set as primary; we can't purge old ciphertext so we'll rewrap active secrets. rough commands:
```
gcloud kms keys versions create  --key=ingest-wrap --keyring=ingest --location=us
# run rewrap job that reads old ciphertext and outputs new ciphertext with primary version
./tools/rewrap --input-bucket=gs://partner-logs --key=projects/redwood/.../ingest-wrap --out-bucket=gs://partner-logs-rewrapped
```
I'll coordinate the rewrap job; estimate 2h for initial batch.

sam: opened a quick PR to redact payloads at the ingestion step and to prevent full-body logs from being archived. Also adding a CI check to fail if payloads >1KB unredacted.

elisabeth: I'll add an audit forwarder rule to ship all Cloud KMS Decrypt events for the ingest-wrap key to security-logs and set retention to 90 days. Also adding an alert for any decrypts outside the usual ingest service identity.

nina: owners and ETA: devon (revocation + key-version create + temporary IAM deny) — now → 1h; devon+sam (rewrap job + verify) — kickoff in 1h, run for 2–3h; sam (pipeline patch) — PR in 30m, rollout after rewrap to avoid breakage; elisabeth (audit + alerts) — in 45m; nina (partner comms, legal) — draft in 1h.

devon: added temp deny binding to project IAM to block partner pipeline writes. logging shows writes stopped at 03:18 UTC. leaving an allow rule only for the minimal inbox service account.

sam: found two CI job logs in partner repo that included full payload lines — archiving snippets to evidence bucket and redacting in-situ. will scrub copies and keep hashes for investigation.

nina: good catch. after rewrap we need to rotate any downstream tokens that referenced these secrets. create a small runbook checklist for app owners to rotate secrets and confirm no stale copies.

elisabeth: note for post-incident: add automated detector that looks for KMS-wrapped blobs with high-entropy base64 inside (we got a decent signal from the scanner) and link to remediation playbook.

nina: agree. I'll post an incident summary to #incidents and follow up with legal + partner ops. Thanks all — update here as you make progress. :white_check_mark:
